---
title: "Marginal summaries and joint direction probabilities"
subtitle: "1.10 · joint laws after the postrank theory book, ch. 9, and a posterior with two bumps"
description: "Dependence and non-normal posterior shape can change direction probabilities without changing marginal means."
---

Outside a jointly normal posterior, marginal means no longer settle $\pi_{AB} = \Pr(\theta_A > \theta_B \mid Y)$: identical margins can reverse $\pi_{AB}$ from 1/3 to 2/3, and skewness can flip mean against direction.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Law 1.** Uniform 1/3 margins (means 1.00) give $\pi_{AB}$ = 1/3, $\pi_{BA}$ = 2/3; at w = .20, A's mean .120 exceeds B's 0 while $\pi_{AB}$ = .392.
- **Law 2.** Re-pairing the same margins raises $\pi_{AB}$ to 2/3.
- **Independent.** Every pair once: margins stay 1/3 with tie probability 1/3, so $\pi_{AB}$ = $\pi_{BA}$ = 1/3 (sum 2/3).
- **Always equal.** Same margins, with A always equal to B ($\pi_{AB}$ = $\pi_{BA}$ = 0).
- **w .50.** Equal bump weights give mean .450 and $\pi_{AB}$ = .620; open **Method and details** for the flip range (.10 to .30).

